The analysis considers a 5-MW composite wind turbine blade made of T300/QY8911 composite material.
The maximum internal stress in the composite blades is found to be 718 MPa using finite element analysis.
The ultimate stress of the composite material is 1548 MPa.
The fatigue life cycles are calculated using the S-N curve model with parameters a = 1.816, b = 8.097, and m = 1.
The gamma process has three key properties: X(t) = 0 at t = 0, independent increments, and X(t) - X(s) follows a gamma distribution for t > s.
The probability density function of the gamma process is given by Ga(x|v,u) = (v^u/Γ(v))x^(v-1)e^(-ux) for x > 0.
The failure probability is calculated as F(t) = P{D ≥ Dcr} = Γ(v(t),uDcr)/Γ(v(t)), where Dcr is the critical fatigue damage level.
The numerical results show the fatigue damage grows rapidly in the first 2 years, then increases gradually until around 20 years when it becomes unstable again.
The failure probability reaches around 90% when the fatigue damage exceeds the critical level of 70-95%.
The proposed stochastic modeling approach can be used to assist in the inspection and maintenance planning for composite wind turbine blades.
The manufacturing cost of composite blades is about 15-20% of the total wind turbine production cost.
Offshore wind turbines typically have a design life of 25-30 years.
Fatigue is one of the most critical mechanical damage mechanisms in layered composite wind turbine blades.
The gamma process is suitable for modeling gradual damage processes like fatigue, corrosion, and wear.
The stochastic fatigue damage model can give reliable results for time-dependent reliability analysis of composite blades.
